title: Who owns result-job completion?
intro: Current source-supported obligations and an unselected regrouping proposal. Boxes denote in-process responsibilities, not packages or deployment containers. Graph views start at the dark Start here node; sequences start at their first message. Proposals and missing transfer knowledge are labelled explicitly. The completion spec carries the durable current contract; the Grove task carries comparison records and gaps.

discussion.title: Signal and resource transfer decides the proposed boundary
discussion.status: Closed undetermined; baseline retained, target and migration unselected
discussion.summary: The funded baseline and regrouped I/C/W family was read, but the required comparison remains incomplete. A fresh source reviewer challenged partial-acquisition ownership and the direct native entry/lifetime contract. Result/job association alone does not settle these questions. A narrow current-source continuation precedes the book agreement; no product code or equivalence campaign was run.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Marked partial-acquisition ownership and native entry/lifetime semantics as separate unresolved G1/G3 obligations.
Corrected Mermaid participant syntax and wrapped labels; retained cleanup/signal joining, failure precedence and the separate final CLI write.

diagrams.title: Consumer pairing versus a completion owner
diagrams.caption: B0 is source-supported at 0bdcb1f9ae24db5e9dd499308dd791744e908eb0; R-I/C/W are declared proposals. Solid arrows are calls/outcomes; dotted arrows are file appearance or a stated unmet transfer requirement. O4–O9 remain required inside any regroup. Configuration/worker/build O1–O3/O10 remain in the task's complete obligation map. Package/publication choices and external adoption are unresolved; human usefulness is unassessed.

diagrams.title: Publication, ending and cleanup join before return
diagrams.caption: Representative current ordering projected onto one completion owner, with the proposed ownership transfer explicitly unresolved. Covers S1/S2/S5 and O4–O9; source run/settle establishes order and precedence. The managed program executes within the runner's job; start events and some appearance polls are omitted. Selection/worker ordering is a precondition, not a new managed-process overlap. This sequence neither enumerates all signal interleavings nor establishes candidate implementation preservation.
